title: Ctrl+S in verb editor throws UnauthorizedAccessException (saves to Program Files)
description:
Critical: pressing Ctrl+S (File > Save) in a local-edit verb editor throws System.UnauthorizedAccessException and the app shows the unhandled-exception dialog. The verb code is not saved.

Observed exception:
System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path
'C:\Program Files\Moo Udditor\ANSI Utilities:notify - SRTMoo-0dcc69b6-2d0c-46c7-aeb4-31f9c0d61d9f' is denied.
  at FastColoredTextBoxNS.Text.TextSource.SaveToFile(...)
  at FastColoredTextBoxNS.FastColoredTextBox.SaveToFile(...)
  at Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor.Main.Editor.mnuItemSave_Click(...) in Editor_FileMenu.cs:line 73

Repro:
- Open a verb via the server local-edit flow (e.g. "ANSI Utilities:notify" on world SRTMoo).
- Press Ctrl+S.

ROOT CAUSE (two intertwined defects):
1. Document.Path is set to a non-path identifier. In MooCodeEditorPage's local-edit constructor (Pages/MooCodeEditorPage.cs ~line 74-80):
     var name = $"{verbName} - {worldName}";
     var key  = $"{name}-{Guid.NewGuid()}";
     Editor.Document = new DocumentInfo(key, key, verbName);   // <- path == key
   The DocumentInfo's *path* is set to `key` (a window/document identifier: "<verb> - <world>-<guid>"), not a real file path. mnuItemSave_Click (Editor_FileMenu.cs:72-73) then does:
     if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(page.Document.Path))
        page.SourceEditor.SaveToFile(page.Document.Path, Encoding.Default);
   Because `key` is a RELATIVE path, SaveToFile resolves it against the current working directory = the install dir (C:\Program Files\Moo Udditor), which is not writable for standard users (we now install to 64-bit Program Files) -> UnauthorizedAccessException.

2. The name contains characters illegal in Windows file paths. MOO verb references use object:verb syntax, so `verbName` = "ANSI Utilities:notify" contains a colon. Even in a writable directory, ':' is treated as an NTFS alternate-data-stream separator; other refs can contain \ / * ? " < > | as well. Any filename derived from a verb reference must be sanitized.

EXPECTED / FIX DIRECTION:
- A local-edit verb document has no on-disk file. Ctrl+S on such a document should NOT write the document key to disk. Preferred: Ctrl+S on a verb page performs the verb UPLOAD back to the server (the existing LocalEditUploader flow), not a FastColoredTextBox file save.
- If/when saving to disk is intended (e.g. Save As, or a working copy), it must (a) use a writable location (%APPDATA%\Moo Udditor or Path.GetTempPath()) and (b) sanitize the filename of all Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() (notably ':').
- Stop assigning `key` to DocumentInfo.Path. Either leave Path empty (so Save routes to Save-As) or assign a proper sanitized, writable path. Distinguish "verb document (upload target)" from "on-disk file document" so Save does the right thing per type.

Affected files: Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor/Main/Editor_FileMenu.cs (mnuItemSave_Click ~line 68-85), Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor/Pages/MooCodeEditorPage.cs (~line 74-80, DocumentInfo path = key), DocumentInfo model, and the local-edit upload path (Communication/OutOfBand/LocalEditUploader.cs).

Severity: critical — crashes via unhandled exception and loses the user's verb edits on a primary, very common action (save). Surfaced by the move to installing under Program Files (non-writable CWD), but the underlying path/identifier confusion is the real bug.

Source: user bug report with full stack trace (assembly version 1.0.26158.7).
notes:
Save-location decision: the default root for new save files should be the user's My Documents folder (Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments / Personal), e.g. a 'Moo Udditor' subfolder under My Documents (which is user-writable, unlike the Program Files install dir). The Save As dialog's InitialDirectory should default there, and filenames must still be sanitized of Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars (notably ':'). Note this is distinct from per-user app data (config/snippets/worlds/logs), which lives in %APPDATA%/Moo Udditor; user-facing saved .moo files belong under My Documents.
CLARIFICATION (supersedes 'fix direction' item 1 in the description): Ctrl+S is INTENDED to save a COPY of the verb code to local disk. It is NOT meant to upload to the server (that is a separate action). So the correct fix is: keep Ctrl+S as a file save, but fix WHERE and WHAT it saves. Because a freshly local-edited verb document has no real on-disk path yet, the current code wrongly uses the window 'key' as Document.Path. Instead: when Document.Path is not a real saved file, Ctrl+S routes to Save As, with the dialog InitialDirectory defaulting to My Documents/Moo Udditor and a suggested file name = the sanitized verb reference (replace Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, notably ':') with a .moo extension. After the user saves once, store the chosen real path in Document.Path so subsequent Ctrl+S overwrites that file silently. Never assign the window key to DocumentInfo.Path.
close_reason: Fixed: stopped storing the window key in DocumentInfo.Path (root cause of the relative-path save into Program Files); Ctrl+S now saves a local copy via Save As defaulting to My Documents/Moo Udditor with a sanitized filename, overwriting silently after first save. Saves go through TrySaveToFile (logs + MessageBox, no crash); PromptForSave (close prompt) hardened identically; SanitizeFileName handles invalid chars, trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names. Independently reviewed; builds clean.

title: Snippet autocomplete matches longer snippet first
description:
Critical: during autocomplete, snippet matching selects a longer snippet over the exact/shorter one. Typing a token matches a snippet that merely has it as a prefix instead of the snippet that exactly matches.

Repro:
- Type "for" -> matches the "Fork" snippet instead of the "for" snippet.
- Type "else" -> matches the "elseif" snippet instead of the "else" snippet.

Expected:
- An exact match should win over a longer prefix match. Typing "for" should select "for", "else" should select "else". Longer snippets (Fork, elseif) should only be offered when the typed text is actually a prefix of only those, or ranked below the exact match.

Notes:
- Likely a snippet match ordering/selection issue in the autocomplete matching logic (see Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/Autocomplete and Snippets handling). Candidate ordering should prioritize exact matches, then shortest/most-specific, rather than first/longest.
- Case sensitivity may also be involved ("for" vs "Fork").

Source: user report.
close_reason: Fixed: autocomplete now ranks exact match first, then shortest, then source order; exact matches no longer hidden. 'for'->'for', 'else'->'else'. Implemented in FastColoredTextBox fork (AutocompleteItem.Compare + AutocompleteMenu.DoAutocomplete), independently reviewed, builds clean.

title: Perf: listed-code highlighting is extremely slow (per-token AppendText/ClearUndo/ScrollToEnd)
description: From udd-z5p. WriteStyledCodeLine calls consoleSim.WriteWithStyle once per token segment; each routes to FCTB AppendText (InsertTextCommand + Invalidate) plus ConsoleWindowEmulator's per-call ClearUndo() and ScrollToEnd(). A highlighted line has ~10-20 segments vs a plain line's 1, so highlighting does an order of magnitude more expensive append ops per line; with the read pump marshaling each line synchronously to the UI thread, a long verb blocks the UI ~20s before anything paints.
design: Add ConsoleWindowEmulator.WriteStyledSegments(IReadOnlyList<(string Text, Style Style)>): wrap in BeginUpdate/EndUpdate, append the whole line's concatenated text ONCE (single InsertTextCommand), then apply each segment's Style to its sub-range via GetRange(Place,Place).SetStyle, and call ClearUndo()+ScrollToEnd() ONCE. WriteStyledCodeLine builds (text,Style) segments and calls it once per line (+ one Write(newline)). Reduces per-line append count from N(tokens) to ~2, matching normal output perf.
acceptance_criteria: Listing a long verb with highlighting on renders about as fast as normal output (no multi-second stall). Colors unchanged. Build clean; existing tests green.
close_reason: Fixed. New ConsoleWindowEmulator.WriteStyledSegments inserts the whole code line once (single AppendText) then applies each token's Style to its sub-range, with BeginUpdate/EndUpdate and a single ClearUndo+ScrollToEnd. WriteStyledCodeLine now calls it once per line instead of WriteWithStyle per token. Per-line append count drops from N(tokens) to ~2, matching normal output perf. Build clean; 375 Editor tests pass. Live speed to be confirmed.

title: FCTB Hotkeys.Parse throws on net8: legacy key abbreviations (Ins/Del/PgUp/PgDn) rejected by KeysConverter
description: After the net8 retarget, opening a terminal (and any FCTB control) throws System.ArgumentException 'Requested value Ins was not found' from HotkeysMapping.Parse -> KeysConverter.ConvertFromString. .NET Framework's KeysConverter accepted abbreviated key names (Ins, Del, PgUp, PgDn) but .NET 8's only accepts full Keys enum names (Insert, Delete, PageUp, PageDown). The FCTB default hotkeys (FastColoredTextBox.cs:936 DefaultValue) and the designer .resx copies (consoleSim.Hotkeys, TextInput.Hotkeys) use the abbreviations, so Parse throws and the terminal/editor cannot be constructed.
design: Make HotkeysMapping.Parse (FastColoredTextBox/Input/Hotkeys.cs) tolerant: normalize legacy key-name abbreviations to full Keys names per '+'-separated segment BEFORE KeysConverter.ConvertFromString. Map Ins->Insert, Del->Delete, PgUp->PageUp, PgDn->PageDown (case-insensitive). One central fix covers the DefaultValue string, the .resx-stored strings, and any saved configs. Regression test in FastColoredTextBox.Tests parsing a string with all four abbreviations + combos.
acceptance_criteria: HotkeysMapping.Parse accepts Ins/Del/PgUp/PgDn (and Shift+/Ctrl+ combos) mapping to Keys.Insert/Delete/PageUp/PageDown without throwing. Opening a terminal no longer throws. Solution builds; FCTB tests + full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed: HotkeysMapping.Parse now normalizes legacy key abbreviations (Ins->Insert, Del->Delete, PgUp->PageUp, PgDn->PageDown) per +-separated segment before KeysConverter.ConvertFromString, which on net8 only accepts full Keys enum names. Covers the FCTB DefaultValue, the designer .resx hotkey strings, and saved configs in one place. 2 regression tests added; FCTB 32 tests, full suite 614 pass.

title: Refactor edgerunner-org-moo-query send_reply/send_error to use core MCP framework send (fixes auth-key=0 reply drop)
description: send_reply (line 443) and send_error (line 465) hand-roll the MCP wire format via notify('#$#'...) and stamp session.key, which resolves to 0 on EdgeRunner cores (the negotiated client key is on .authentication_key). The core MCP framework already does key-stamping, package-prefix, and multiline data* chunking via connection:send(message, parse_send_args(...)) — exactly as #215:send_* and the simpleedit reference (#230) use it. Refactor both verbs to delegate to the framework instead of reinventing the wire format. Root cause of member-completion popup never appearing for $foo: contexts (replies discarded by McpMessageDispatcher key check).

title: Member autocomplete popup never opens on first trigger (results land after menu closed)
description: When the user types 'obj:' / 'obj.' / '$name:' the trigger keystroke runs DoAutocomplete while the member fetch is still in flight; GetMemberItems returns empty, no static item matches the fragment, and AutocompleteMenu closes (Count==0 -> Menu.Close). When the fetch lands, the MooCodeEditorPage menuRefresh callback only re-shows a VISIBLE menu (menu is { Visible: true }), so the popup never opens — user must type another character. Fix: when the menu is closed and the caret still sits in a member context with non-empty fetched items, open the menu (Show(false)) from the refresh callback, guarded by editor focus. Also: MemberCompletionController swallows all provider failures silently with no logging anywhere in the Editor project — add an optional diagnostic callback invoked on fetch failure and core-name validation failure, wired to NLog in MooCodeEditorPage, so field failures are diagnosable.
notes: Scope addition: McpMessageDispatcher.cs:83 silently drops messages whose auth key mismatches Session.Key — log a WARN naming message name + both keys. This silent drop cost a full debugging session (server sent key 0; replies dropped; queries timed out). Root cause of user's $network: failure was server-side: core session object stores auth key in a property other than .key (send_reply emitted 0).
close_reason: Popup-show fix + dispatcher WARN + diagnostic callback implemented, reviewed, approved

title: Autocomplete does not open for $name member operands ($network:)
description: MemberOperandResolver only resolves #N literals and 'this' for Verb/Property contexts; $name operands (e.g. $network:) return null and MemberCompletionController silently skips member completion — no query is sent, popup never opens. Fix: resolve $name client-side via GetPropertyValueAsync(#0, name) (prop-value op returns {"t":1,"v":"#N"}), cache name→objnum with TTL, then run the normal verb/prop fetch. Covers both $name: and $name. forms. No server-side changes needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: MCP multiline content double-spaced: parser retains transport newline in continuation values
description:
Surfaced testing simpleedit @edit: verb code opens in the editor with a blank line between every line (unusable).

Root cause: the OOB transport delivers each line with a trailing newline (MudClientSession.FlushLine appends "
"). RootMessageProcessor strips only the #$# prefix, not the newline, so McpMessageParser.FeedLine receives lines ending in "
". ProcessMultilineLine preserves the continuation value literally (to keep indentation), INCLUDING the trailing "
", then assembles with string.Join("
", lines) -> each line becomes 'code
' and the join inserts another '
', producing a blank line between every content line. Single-line messages are unaffected because ProcessNormalLine goes through SplitMessageIntoWords which trims.

Fix: strip a single trailing line terminator (one '
', plus a preceding '' if present) at the top of McpMessageParser.FeedLine before dispatching to the normal/multiline handlers, so the parser tolerates the transport newline. Add a parser test feeding newline-terminated continuation lines and asserting single-newline join.
close_reason: Verified working against EdgeRunner: @edit opens the verb, code is single-spaced with indentation intact, and round-trip save programs the verb. (Blank-line stripping confirmed to be MOO server compile/decompile behavior, not a client bug.)

title: Network read loop splits long OOB lines across 10KB chunks, breaking MCP multiline
description:
Regression surfaced by enabling dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit (udd-wm8): @edit on a connected MOO opens no editor.

Root cause (confirmed via Moo Udditor.log): MudClientSession.ReadFromConnection reads in 10240-byte chunks and calls FlushCommandBuffer() after EVERY chunk (MudClientSession.cs:342). FlushCommandBuffer (line 440) flushes any unterminated partial line (needed so no-newline prompts display). When a long line spans a 10KB read boundary it gets emitted as two channel messages: the first half (still #$#-prefixed) and the remainder (no prefix). Mid-MCP-multiline, RootMessageProcessor delegates the prefix-less remainder to McpOobHandler, whose parser is in multiline state and returns Error on a line that is neither '* ...' nor ': ...', which resets the parser and sets Finished=true -> the entire simpleedit content message is aborted -> no editor. Log shows the 'Resetting message processor' cascade starting exactly where a long verb line ('player:tell(...)') was truncated to '...content: p'.

Fix: in ReadFromConnection, only call FlushCommandBuffer() when the read drained the socket (bytes < buffer.Length); a full-buffer read means more of the current line is likely still coming, so keep accumulating until the newline (FlushLine) so multi-chunk lines reassemble intact. Prompts (short reads) still flush. Stream-agnostic (also fixes TLS) and testable with a scripted stream.

Affects all connections (core networking). Pre-existing latent issue adjacent to docs/terminal-buffer-cutoff-investigation.md Issue 3; exposed now because @edit routes through MCP multiline.
close_reason: Verified working against EdgeRunner: @edit opens the verb, code is single-spaced with indentation intact, and round-trip save programs the verb. (Blank-line stripping confirmed to be MOO server compile/decompile behavior, not a client bug.)

title: Autocomplete popup crashes at high editor zoom (no font-size ceiling)
description:
Typing with autocomplete open after zooming the editor up throws System.ArgumentException 'Parameter is not valid' from System.Drawing.Font.GetHeight, via AutocompleteListView.ItemHeight -> ApplyZoom -> DoAutocomplete (AutocompleteMenu.cs:194/325/399).

Root cause: AutocompletePopupMetrics.Compute (FastColoredTextBox/AutocompletePopupMetrics.cs) floors the effective font size at MinFontSizeInPoints (6pt) but applies NO upper ceiling. The editor's own FastColoredTextBox.DoZoom guards 'points < 1f || points > 300f', but FastColoredTextBox.Zoom's setter stores the raw zoom field even when DoZoom bails out of range. So at high zoom tb.Zoom keeps climbing while the editor font caps at 300pt; the popup recomputes baseFont(9pt) * zoom/100 unbounded and asks GDI+ for a degenerate (huge) font. GDI+ returns a Font with an invalid native handle, so Font.Height throws.

Repro: zoom the editor up substantially, then type so autocomplete fires. Also reproduced after tabbing away/back with an already-high zoom.

Fix: clamp the computed font size to a sane maximum (mirror the editor's 300pt cap) in AutocompletePopupMetrics.Compute, plus a unit test for the high-zoom cap.
design: Build effective font from family name (not FontFamily object) to decouple lifetime; snapshot family name/size/style at assignment time while the source font is still valid.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (verified by reproduction test ShowMenu_ThenZoom_ThenReshow_DoesNotCrash): AutocompleteListView built its effective (zoomed) font from baseFont.FontFamily. When the ToolStripControlHost/ambient-font machinery pushes its own Font onto the list view (through the overridden Font setter, which resets baseFont) and WinForms later disposes that pushed font, every font sharing its FontFamily is invalidated -> Font.Height throws 'Parameter is not valid'. Triggered on ANY zoom change followed by the menu becoming visible (DoSelectedVisible/DoAutocomplete). The missing font-size ceiling (original hypothesis) was NOT the cause; that clamp was kept as a secondary safety.

FIX (FastColoredTextBox/AutocompleteMenu.cs): capture the baseline font identity (family NAME string, point size, style) into immutable fields whenever baseFont is assigned, and rebuild the effective font from the family NAME so each effective font owns its own family and is immune to WinForms disposing the pushed font. Plus defensive guards: try/catch in ApplyZoom font creation and in ItemHeight. Verified: the repro test failed before the fix and passes after; full FCTB test suite 12/12 green; main app builds.
close_reason: Fixed: ApplyZoom disposed the live base.Font when Control.Font ignored an equal-by-value reassignment. Now only swaps+disposes when the font actually differs. Verified by forced-paint repro test (host-crash before, passes after) and confirmed working in-app by user.

title: CI: run dotnet.yml on windows-latest (WinForms net8.0-windows can't build/test on Linux)
description: GitHub Actions workflow ran on ubuntu-latest; restoring/building the net8.0-windows WinForms projects on Linux fails with 'set the EnableWindowsTargeting property to true'. The app and its test projects are WinForms (net8.0-windows) and require Windows to build AND run tests, so the runner must be Windows. title: Hover tooltips for Moo literal constants (type codes + error tostr), live-query-with-fallback
description: Add hover tooltips for Moo literal constants. Type constants (NUM/INT/OBJ/STR/ERR/LIST/FLOAT/MAP/ANON/WAIF/BOOL) show their numeric typeof code (e.g. 'NUM => 0'); error constants (E_*) show their tostr() message (e.g. 'E_PERM => Permission denied'). One comprehensive baked-in table (dialect-agnostic). Also extend the query provider with two methods to fetch a constant's raw value and tostr() live, with the client attempting the query and falling back to the baked-in table when unsupported/offline. SDWC does NOT support constant queries (returns unsupported), so today the hover always uses the baked-in table; the live plumbing is future-facing with no SDWC wire changes.
design:
A. New BuiltinConstantDocs (mirror BuiltinFunctionDocs: JSON resource Resources/builtin-constant-docs.json + Lazy<IReadOnlyDictionary> + GetTooltipText). Entry per constant: kind (type|error|bool) + display string. Types -> numeric typeof code (INT/NUM=0, OBJ=1, STR=2, ERR=3, LIST=4, FLOAT=9, MAP=10, ANON=12, WAIF=13, BOOL=14 — VERIFY against ToastStunt during impl). Errors -> tostr() message (E_NONE 'No error'=0 ... E_FLOAT 'Floating-point arithmetic error'=15, plus ToastStunt E_FILE/E_EXEC/E_INTRPT). Add public Moo.IsConstant(name) (ConstantSet is private). GetTooltipText(name) returns 'NAME => display'.
B. Hover: in MooCodeEditor.ClassifyHoveredMember add HoverMemberKind.Constant branch (IDENTIFIER && Moo.IsConstant(text)) BEFORE the bare-local fallback and after the function check; in MooEditor_ToolTipNeeded render 'NAME => display'. Use the same ShowToolTipAbove path.
C. IMooWorldQueryProvider gains GetConstantValueAsync(string name, CancellationToken) (raw value, for types) and GetConstantToStrAsync(string name, CancellationToken) (tostr, for errors). Implement: SdwcQueryProvider -> return null (UNSUPPORTED, no new SDWC command/token); MCP provider -> null; CachingMooWorldQueryProvider + MooWorldQueryService -> delegate (pass-through null when unsupported, no caching of null); test fakes -> return configured values. Hover resolution: attempt live via the editor's provider accessor (types call GetConstantValueAsync, errors call GetConstantToStrAsync); on null/exception/offline (no provider) fall back to BuiltinConstantDocs. Fast fallback (no timeout) because SDWC returns null immediately and offline has no provider.
D. Tests in Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor.Tests: BuiltinConstantDocs (type->value, error->message, bool, unknown->null), Moo.IsConstant, and a hover-resolution helper preferring live then falling back (with a fake provider). FCTB tooltip paint not unit-testable.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a type constant shows 'NAME => <typeof code>'; hovering an error shows 'NAME => <tostr message>'; non-constants unaffected. IMooWorldQueryProvider has the two new methods; SdwcQueryProvider/MCP return null; service/caching delegate; offline + SDWC both fall back to the baked-in table with no hover lag. New tests pass; full solution builds clean; all suites green.
close_reason: Implemented. BuiltinConstantDocs (JSON resource, mirrors BuiltinFunctionDocs) with authoritative ToastStunt values: types -> typeof code (NUM=>0 etc.), errors -> tostr message (E_PERM=>Permission denied etc.), true/false. Moo.IsConstant added. MooCodeEditor HoverMemberKind.Constant branch gated on IDENTIFIER|ERROR|BOOLEAN tokens (error consts lex as ERROR, bools as BOOLEAN -- corrected from IDENTIFIER-only). IMooWorldQueryProvider gains GetConstantValueAsync/GetConstantToStrAsync; SdwcQueryProvider+McpQueryProvider return null (unsupported, no wire change), registry/caching delegate, fakes configurable. ConstantHoverResolver.ResolveConstantDisplay (live-then-fallback) testable helper; hover tries live then falls back to baked-in (always baked-in today). 678 tests pass (60 new Editor + 4 new Common); solution builds clean.

title: Retarget all 14 projects from .NET 6 to .NET 8 (net8.0 / net8.0-windows)
description: Move the whole solution from net6.0 to net8.0 (LTS, VS2022-supported; clears NETSDK1138 out-of-support warning). 5 Windows projects net6.0-windows->net8.0-windows (FastColoredTextBox, FastColoredTextBox.Tests, Moo.Editor, Moo.Editor.Tests, Moo.Udditor); 9 non-Windows projects net6.0->net8.0 (ANTLR4.Tools.Common, Common, Messaging, MooText, Mud.Common(+Tests), Mud.Communication(+Tests), Mud.MCP(+Tests)).

No package-version bumps, no LangVersion changes, no C#12 adoption — unless a package genuinely fails to restore/build on net8, in which case bump only that package and report it. HtmlRenderer NU1701 warnings will persist (pre-existing, benign). Verify with dotnet restore + full solution build + all 5 test suites green.

title: File>Load into current editor + reset modified-line gutter on save/upload/load
description: Add a File menu 'Load' item (after Open) that opens a file dialog and REPLACES the current code editor's contents with the chosen file, guarded by a confirm prompt if there are unsaved changes; grayed out when the current page is not a MooCodeEditorPage. Also reset the modified-line gutter indicator (FCTB line.IsChanged painted with ChangedLineColor) so nothing shows modified after: (a) saving a plain .moo file not bound to a session verb, (b) uploading from a session-bound verb window, and (c) loading a file via the new Load item.
design: Mechanism: the modified-line gutter bar is FCTB line.IsChanged rendered with ChangedLineColor (EditorChangedLineColor, default Yellow); setting SourceEditor.IsChanged=false clears all line flags (FCTB.IsChanged setter -> lines.ClearIsChanged()). Confirmed gap: MooEditorPage.UploadSource (MooEditorPage.cs:124-132) sets IsChanged=false on success but never Invalidate()s, so cleared flags don't repaint. PART A (Load): new ToolStripMenuItem after mnuItemOpenFile in File menu DropDownItems (Editor.Designer.cs). Enable only when CurrentPage is MooCodeEditorPage, set in Editor_MenuConfiguration.UpdateMenus alongside isMooCodeEditor. Handler in Editor_FileMenu.cs after mnuItemOpenFile_Click: OpenFileDialog same filter as Open (.moo/.txt/.md/all). On OK: if page.SourceEditor.IsChanged, MessageBox Yes/No confirm discarding unsaved changes (abort on No); set page.SourceEditor.Text = File.ReadAllText(path); then MarkAsUnmodified (clean baseline). try/catch with error MessageBox like TrySaveToFile. PART B (reset helper): add MooEditorPage.MarkAsUnmodified() => { SourceEditor.IsChanged=false; SourceEditor.Invalidate(); }. Call it: in UploadSource on successful Upload (adds missing Invalidate); after successful TrySaveToFile in the save path; and from the Load handler. Route all three through the one helper so clear+repaint are always paired.
acceptance_criteria: File>Load present after Open; grayed out unless a code editor is active; replaces current editor content; prompts before discarding unsaved changes; loaded file shows clean gutter. After saving a plain .moo file the modified bars clear. After a successful upload the modified bars clear (repaints). Tests: MarkAsUnmodified clears IsChanged; UploadSource success clears IsChanged; Load enable predicate true only for MooCodeEditorPage. Full solution builds clean; all test projects green.
close_reason: Implemented. File>Load (mnuItemLoadFile) after Open: enabled only for MooCodeEditorPage, OpenFileDialog (Open's filter), Yes/No guard when SourceEditor.IsChanged, replaces buffer via File.ReadAllText, then MarkAsUnmodified (clean baseline); try/catch error box. New MooEditorPage.MarkAsUnmodified() = IsChanged=false + Invalidate(); called from UploadSource success (adds the missing repaint that was the upload bug), after successful TrySaveToFile (save + save-as), and from Load. Solution builds clean; all 612 tests across 5 projects pass. Merged to master.

title: Tools menu: Flush Editor Cache action + live Editor Cache TTL setting + move Options
description: Wire the (already-added, uncommitted) Tools > Flush Editor Cache menu item to flush ALL cached provider/query data across every open editor page and terminal, so stale values / newly-added verbs can be force-refreshed. Add a user-configurable 'Editor Cache TTL (seconds)' on Options > Code Features that controls how long cached values live, applied LIVE to already-open editors/connections. Move the Options item from the View menu into the Tools menu, after Flush Editor Cache, with a separator between them.
design: FLUSH: fill flushEditorCacheToolStripMenuItem_Click (Editor.cs:265). Add MemberCompletionController.ClearCache() (clear _cache, _propertyObjectCache, _currentPlayerCache, inflight key/chain under _stateLock). Expose via MooCodeEditorPage.FlushCache(). Handler: for each WindowManager page OfType<MooCodeEditorPage> call FlushCache(); for each OfType<TerminalPage> call Terminal.QueryProviders.Clear() (MooWorldQueryService.Clear already exists -> CachingMooWorldQueryProvider.Clear). TTL (single setting drives BOTH caches, live): add Settings.EditorCacheTtlSeconds (int, default 60) + SaveTo/Load/Clone/CopyFrom (mirror EditorAutocompleteDelay). title: SDWC: SUPPORT handshake — declare client support + detect server abilities
description: Implement the SDWC SUPPORT handshake in SdwcOobHandler. Replace the dome-client-user capability hack with the real handshake: parse the server's inbound '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%verbs|props|PROP-OVERLAY|VERB-OVERLAY|SUPPORT' broadcast into a stored ability set, register SdwcQueryProvider off that (gated on a queryable ability), and send the client's own '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%' declaration exactly once. Out of scope: @dome-client-user host/ip reply, NOWRAP changes, new payload features (VERBS/PROPS/overlays already exist). Protocol refs: docs/MOO-SETUP.md + SDWC-OOB.md (SindomeCorp/dome-client).
design: Flow: server auto-broadcasts SUPPORT on connect -> client parses+stores caps + registers provider (detect) -> client sends '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%' ONCE (declare). New SdwcServerCapabilities value object: typed accessors SupportsVerbs/SupportsProps/SupportsVerbOverlay/SupportsPropOverlay (case-insensitive vs tokens verbs/props/VERB-OVERLAY/PROP-OVERLAY) + raw IReadOnlySet<string> (preserves unknown/future tokens). Stored on SdwcOobHandler as ServerCapabilities (nullable until first SUPPORT; last-wins). In ProcessMessage special-case 'SDWC%%SUPPORT%%' BEFORE the JSON-correlation HandleResponse path; payload split on '|', trim, drop empties. Remove CapabilitySignal='dome-client-user' const + branch; provider registration moves to SUPPORT path, gated on >=1 queryable ability (verbs/props/VERB-OVERLAY/PROP-OVERLAY), once-only. Outbound: on first SUPPORT, send via IClientTerminal.SendOutOfBandLine yielding exactly '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%'; _declarationSent bool under _registrationLock makes it once-only; later broadcasts refresh caps, no re-send. OnDisconnected also clears ServerCapabilities + resets _declarationSent. Unhandled dome-client-user line now returns false (may display; acceptable). Existing VERBS/PROPS/overlay correlation untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound SUPPORT -> ServerCapabilities populated (typed + raw, case-insensitive, unknown tokens kept) + provider registered when a queryable ability present; only-SUPPORT/no-queryable -> caps stored, provider NOT registered. Outbound '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%' sent EXACTLY once (fake terminal captures SendOutOfBandLine); 2nd broadcast refreshes caps, no 2nd send. dome-client-user returns false (no registration). Existing VERBS/PROPS/overlay correlation still works. OnDisconnected resets caps + declaration flag. Communication.Tests green; solution builds clean.

SdwcOobHandler: removed dome-client-user hack; parses inbound SDWC%%SUPPORT%% into ServerCapabilities (last-wins), registers SdwcQueryProvider only when a queryable ability present, sends outbound '#$# SDWC%%SUPPORT%%' exactly once (verified wire line), OnDisconnected resets caps+flag. title: Hover tooltips do not work for bare this/player/caller (and other bare resolvable operands)
description:
Hovering the bare keyword this, player, or caller shows NO tooltip. Only hovering a MEMBER on them works (e.g. player:foo -> hovering foo resolves the player base via the chained-hover path from udd-e7j). Hovering the operand keyword itself shows nothing.

Root cause: MooCodeEditor.ClassifyHoveredMember (Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/Controls/MooCodeEditor.cs:187-229) only produces hover content for: (a) a standalone CORE_REFERENCE token ($name -> property on #0), (b) an IDENTIFIER preceded by ':'/'.'  (a member on a chain), or (c) an IDENTIFIER followed by '(' (a builtin function). A bare this/player/caller is an IDENTIFIER that is NOT preceded by a separator and NOT followed by '(', so it falls through to (HoverMemberKind.None, ...) and no tooltip is shown. The same gap affects a bare #N object literal.

Desired: hovering a bare resolvable operand resolves it to its object and shows that object. Scope for THIS bead: this, player, caller, and #N object-literal operands, resolved by their DEFAULT meaning (this -> ContextObjectId; player/caller -> GetCurrentPlayerAsync; #N -> that object). Reassignment-aware values (e.g. 'player = #23' earlier in the verb) are explicitly OUT of scope here and belong to udd-2s4 (flow-aware lazy reassignment tracking), which will later enhance this same hover path. Bare LOCAL variables are likewise deferred to udd-2s4.

Resolution reuses the existing ChainExpressionEvaluator: build a ChainDescriptor with the appropriate base (This/Player/Caller/ObjectLiteral) and no steps, evaluate to a MooObjectId. This is a new hover INTENT (resolve-and-show-object) distinct from the existing verb-doc / property-value member fetch, so it needs a new hover kind on the MooHoverRequest path (e.g. MooHoverMemberKind.Object) and a branch in MooCodeEditorPage.FetchHoverContentAsync that displays the resolved object (its #N, and its .name via GetPropertyValueAsync when available) instead of fetching a member.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Hovering bare 'this' shows the resolved object (ContextObjectId) when known; no tooltip (not an error) when ContextObjectId is unset. 2. Hovering bare 'player' or 'caller' shows the connected player object via GetCurrentPlayerAsync. 3. Hovering a bare #N object literal shows that object. 4. Tooltip displays at least the object number, plus the object's .name when cheaply available; degrades gracefully when not. 5. No regression to existing hover: $name core refs, members on chains (incl. player:foo / this:bar), and builtin functions still work. 6. Bare local variables and reassignment-aware values remain no-source here (deferred to udd-2s4). 7. Unit coverage for the new classification/resolution seam where testable (mirror the udd-e7j ExtractAtSeparator tests / ChainExpressionEvaluator base-resolution tests).
notes: Split out of udd-2s4 per Thad: fix the hover bug first, independently of the flow-aware reassignment feature. Builds directly on udd-e7j (chained-expression hover). Related: udd-lu1/this-player-caller-resolution design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-this-player-caller-resolution-design.md) which specified player/caller hover for the MEMBER case; this bead adds the BARE-operand case. udd-2s4 will later layer reassignment-aware values onto the same path.

New pure ChainExtractor.ClassifyBareResolvableOperand maps #N/this/player/caller to a chain base (bare locals + $name -> null, deferred/handled elsewhere); ClassifyHoveredMember restructured to detect a bare resolvable operand not in member position -> new Object hover intent; page resolves it via the existing ChainExpressionEvaluator and displays => #N (name), name best-effort via .name. Default resolution only (this->ContextObjectId, player/caller->GetCurrentPlayerAsync); reassignment-aware values remain udd-2s4. title: Autocomplete popup does not select the first alphabetically-matching option (properties/verbs)
description:
As the user types, the autocomplete popup should keep its alphabetically-sorted list and highlight the FIRST alphabetically-matching option. Instead, for member completions (properties confirmed, verbs presumed) the highlighted/selected item is often not the first alphabetic match. We thought this was fixed for snippets (udd-45u), but it regresses/persists for properties too.

Repro: connect to a world, trigger member completion on an object (e.g. $obj. for properties or $obj: for verbs), and type a prefix. The selected (focused) row is not the first item alphabetically among the matches.

Suspected root cause: the focus-selection ranking in AutocompleteMenu.cs (FastColoredTextBox/AutocompleteMenu.cs:465-489, the loop that computes bestIndex) ranks matching items 'exact match first, then SHORTEST, then source order' (introduced by udd-45u / commit 83be419 'prefer exact then shortest match'). The 'shortest' tiebreak overrides alphabetical-first: e.g. with members 'name' and 'nz', typing 'n' selects 'nz' (shortest, len 2) rather than 'name' (alphabetically first). Because member lists are already alphabetically sorted (MemberCompletionController.BuildVerbItems/BuildPropertyItems OrderBy name; commit 24d7fb1), the desired behavior is simply: among items returning CompareResult.VisibleAndSelected, prefer an exact (case-insensitive) match, otherwise pick the FIRST in source (already-sorted/alphabetical) order — drop the 'shortest' tiebreak (or make it secondary to source order).

Items in scope: MemberCompletionItem.Compare returns VisibleAndSelected only on prefix match (Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/Autocomplete/MemberCompletionItem.cs:70). The shared ranking in AutocompleteMenu applies to snippets AND members, so any change must be verified to keep the snippet behavior udd-45u wanted (exact-then-prefix) while making prefix selection land on the alphabetically-first match. Confirm verbs exhibit the same symptom.
acceptance_criteria: 1. With an alphabetically-sorted completion list, typing a prefix highlights the FIRST alphabetically-matching item (not the shortest). 2. An exact case-insensitive match still wins over a non-exact prefix match. 3. Verified for properties AND verbs AND snippets (no regression to udd-45u's exact-match preference). 4. Empty fragment (just after ':'/'.') keeps the first item highlighted. 5. Add/extend a unit test around the bestIndex selection logic (or a MemberCompletionItem/AutocompleteMenu test) covering the 'name' vs 'nz' style case.
notes: Related: udd-45u (83be419 prefer exact then shortest match) — this bug is that the 'shortest' rule conflicts with 'first alphabetic match'. Also 24d7fb1 'Sort autocomplete completion items alphabetically' (lists are pre-sorted). Reporter (Thad) wants: list sorted alphabetically + first alphabetically-matching option selected as you type.
close_reason: Fixed: autocomplete focus-selection now prefers exact match, then the ALPHABETICALLY-FIRST prefix match (was 'shortest', which overrode alphabetical order — e.g. members name/nz, typing 'n' selected nz instead of name). Ranking extracted to a pure, unit-tested public helper AutocompleteMatchRanker.SelectBestMatchIndex (FastColoredTextBox) and wired into AutocompleteListView.DoAutocomplete, mapping the picked index back to the visibleItems index. Exact-match-wins (udd-45u: for->for, else->else) preserved. 8 new ranker tests; FCTB 21 + Editor 199 pass; app builds clean. Applies to properties and verbs (shared ranking path).

title: MCP package enable/disable management page (global + per-world)
description:
Add a UI page/dialog where the user can enable or disable each MCP package that Udditor supports, so they can opt out of packages they don't want active.

Why: Udditor advertises/accepts a set of MCP (Mud Client Protocol) packages during negotiation. Users need control over which packages are active rather than always enabling everything.

Scope:
- A new 'MCP Packages' page/dialog (e.g. under the View menu, alongside Theme/Options) that lists every MCP package Udditor supports, each with an enable/disable toggle and a short description.
- Two levels of configuration:
  1. GLOBAL default - applies to all worlds unless overridden.
  2. PER-WORLD override - each world can override the global setting per package. Support tri-state per world: Inherit global / Force enabled / Force disabled.
- Persistence: global defaults in the application config; per-world overrides in the world configuration (Org.Edgerunner.Mud.Common/WorldConfiguration.cs, surfaced via WorldConfigurator/WorldManager). 
- Integration: MCP negotiation (Org.Edgerunner.Mud.MCP - McpClientSessionManager / McpOobHandler / IMcpPackage implementations such as SimpleEditPackage) must only offer/accept packages that are enabled for the connecting world (per-world override else global default). Disabled packages must not be negotiated or handled.
- Discoverability: the supported-package list should be derived from the registered IMcpPackage implementations so it stays in sync as packages are added.

Out of scope: implementing new MCP packages; changing the MCP handshake/negotiation protocol itself beyond filtering by the enabled set.
acceptance_criteria:
- An MCP Packages page can be opened and lists all supported packages with enable/disable controls.
- Global enable/disable of a package persists and takes effect for worlds with no override.
- A world can override any package to Inherit/Enabled/Disabled, persisted with the world config.
- During MCP negotiation for a connection, only packages enabled for that world (override else global) are offered/accepted; disabled packages are not negotiated or handled.
- The package list reflects the actual registered IMcpPackage implementations.

title: McpMessageParser multiline parsing uses wrong data-tag convention
description:
Defect in the udd-q2l deliverable. McpMessageParser's multiline handling assumes the data-tag is the value written after a keyword ending in '*:' (e.g. 'content*: <tag>'). The real MCP 2.1 model is different:

- The inline value after 'content*:' is syntactically required but IGNORED (conventionally "").
- The message line carries a single separate '_data-tag:' keyword whose value is the tag for the WHOLE message.
- Continuation lines are '#$#* <data-tag> <keyword>: <value>' and route to fields BY KEYWORD; multiple multiline fields in one message share the same data-tag.
- Close line is '#$#: <data-tag>'.

Current parser keys its multiline buffers by the (empty) inline value and looks up continuation lines by tag, so real server multiline messages (incl. dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit-content) parse with an empty buffer and the actual content lines are dropped.

Fix: rework ProcessNormalLine/ProcessMultilineLine to (1) mark keywords ending in '*:' as multiline fields keyed by field name, ignoring their inline value, (2) read the single '_data-tag:' simple field as the message tag, (3) route continuation lines by matching tag + keyword, (4) close on ': <tag>'. Add tests covering the canonical MCP 2.1 example.

Also fix docs/mcp2-protocol.md which wrongly states each multiline field uses a different data-tag; per spec there is one _data-tag per message.

Blocks udd-wm8 (simpleedit content/set are multiline).
close_reason: Implemented on feature/mcp-simpleedit: udd-u5v fixes McpMessageParser to the MCP 2.1 _data-tag multiline model; udd-wm8 adds the dns-org-mud-moo-simpleedit package (SimpleEditPackage + SimpleEditUploader + FormatMultilineMessage + WindowManager wiring). 62 MCP tests pass, Udditor builds. title: Code hints + gutter code-action icon in the editor
description:
Today the editor only surfaces raw parser/syntax errors (via ParsingCompleteEventArgs -> ParserMessageDisplayPage). This feature adds a richer in-editor diagnostics/assist layer, in two related parts:

1. Code hints — display more than raw syntax errors: informational/warning hints, suggestions, and contextual diagnostics inline in the code editor windows (e.g. squiggles/markers + hover or inline hint text), layered on top of the existing ANTLR parse results so non-error insights (style, deprecations, unused locals, dialect-specific suggestions) can be shown without being treated as hard errors.

2. Gutter code-action icon — a clickable action affordance (lightbulb-style) drawn in the editor gutter/margin on lines that have an available action. Triggering it opens a menu of context actions such as refactorings (rename, extract, inline, quick-fixes for a hint). Actions are produced by the same diagnostics layer that feeds the hints.

The two parts share a model: a diagnostics/hint provider yields hints (some with attached actions); hints render as markers, actionable lines get the gutter icon, and invoking the icon runs the chosen action.
design: Build on existing pieces: the per-change background parse already raises ParsingCompleteEventArgs; extend that pipeline to emit non-error hints alongside errors instead of only errors. Render hints via FastColoredTextBox styles/markers (the fork already supports custom gutter/margin drawing and bookmark-style icons — same surface used for line markers). The gutter code-action icon is a margin glyph drawn on lines with available actions; clicking it shows a context menu of actions. Define a small provider abstraction (hint -> optional list of code actions) so dialect-specific analyzers (LambdaMoo/ToastStunt/Edgerunner) can contribute. Keep the action execution decoupled from rendering. Reuse the CompletionIconFactory/icon approach for crisp, zoom-aware glyphs (see udd-x6l) if the gutter icon should scale with editor zoom. title: Abstract dev-info query provider (IMooWorldQueryProvider)
description:
Define an abstracted interface, IMooWorldQueryProvider, that provides a uniform mechanism for querying a connected MOO world for developer/introspection information, independent of the underlying wire protocol. Concrete providers (SDWC, and an upcoming MCP package) implement this interface; the client discovers which providers a given world supports and wires the appropriate one to that MUD world session. Editor windows consume the active provider to power code-completion popups and tooltips.

Interface: IMooWorldQueryProvider
Operations (async-first — most are network round-trips, so return Task/Task<T> with CancellationToken support):
- Query the list of verbs on an object.
- Query the list of properties on an object.
- Query the list of known objects.
- Query the list of all child objects of a given object.
- Query the parent of a given object.
- Query detailed information for a specific verb.
- Query detailed information for a specific property.

Provider model / wiring:
- On connect, attempt to determine which query providers the world supports (capability probe / negotiation).
- Select and bind a provider implementation to the MudWorldSession for that connection.
- Expose the bound provider to editor consumers (completion + tooltips). Gracefully degrade when no provider is available.

Implementations (separate beads):
- SDWC OOB protocol implementation — udd-am1 (becomes an implementation of this interface).
- Upcoming MCP package (to be designed) — a second implementation.

Design notes:
- Keep the interface protocol-agnostic; return typed models (verb info, property info, object id) rather than raw protocol payloads.
- Likely lives in the communication/editor-shared layer so both comms implementations and the editor can reference it.

Acceptance:
- IMooWorldQueryProvider exists with async methods for the seven query operations above.
- At least one concrete implementation can be bound to a session (SDWC, udd-am1).
- Provider discovery selects/binds a supported provider per world session.
- Editor can obtain the active provider and query it for completion/tooltip data.

Source: user request. Related implementations: udd-am1 (SDWC) and a future MCP package bead.

title: Support SDWC protocol for verb/property introspection
description:
Implement client support for the SDWC out-of-band protocol so Udditor can query a connected MOO for an object's verbs and properties and consume the JSON metadata it returns. This provides the live introspection backbone for the object/verb browser and world-aware autocomplete features.

Protocol summary (from docs):
- SDWC is an out-of-band protocol carried over standard MOO output using the #$# OOB prefix (same channel Udditor already handles via OutOfBandMessageProcessor).
- Client -> server requests:
  - #$# SDWC%%VERBS%%<objectId>   (request verbs for an object)
  - #$# SDWC%%PROPS%%<objectId>   (request properties for an object)
- Server -> client responses carry JSON payloads:
  - #$# SDWC%%VERBS%%<json>
  - #$# SDWC%%PROPS%%<json>
- Marker families: control lines, payload responses, and metadata/handshake lines. Payloads are valid JSON.
- Capability toggles (server side, via environment) can disable Object Browser / Property Browser / hover overlays. No formal capability negotiation.

Scope:
- Add an SDWC OOB message handler in the communication layer (register with the OOB pipeline, key off the SDWC%% markers).
- Request API to ask for verbs/props of a given object id; parse and surface the JSON responses as typed models.
- Respect server capability toggles where exposed.
- Expose results to consumers (object/verb browser udd-9ge, world-aware autocomplete udd-of6).

Reference docs:
- https://github.com/SindomeCorp/dome-client/blob/main/docs/SDWC-OOB.md
- Repo docs index: https://github.com/SindomeCorp/dome-client/tree/main/docs

Note: enabler/dependency for udd-9ge (Object / verb browser) and udd-of6 (World-aware autocomplete). Source: user request.

title: Terminal: syntax-highlight verb code listed from the MOO (intercept @list output, strip ANSI, re-color)
description:
Add a toggleable option that auto-detects when verb code is being listed in the terminal from the MOO (e.g. @list obj:verb), intercepts it, strips any ANSI coloring the MOO sent, parses the code, and re-displays it using the editor's Moo syntax-highlighting color scheme — so listed code in the terminal looks like code in the editor. Off by default; controlled by a new setting on Options > Code Features.

Trigger: the standard verb-list HEADER line, of the form '#<id>:<verb name, maybe quoted>  <indirect object> <prepstr> <direct object> [<owner name> (#<owner number>), <flags>]'. When a terminal line matches that header, treat the following lines as the verb's code body, capture them until the listing terminates, and apply highlighting to those code lines (and optionally style the header).
design:
Likely touch points (verify during design): incoming text pipeline (Org.Edgerunner.Moo.MooText: MooTextPipeline/MooColorTextProcessor and AnsiManager) feeding MooClientTerminal; the Moo syntax highlighter (Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/SyntaxHighlighting/MooSyntaxHighlightingGuide) for coloring; Settings (new bool, e.g. EditorHighlightListedVerbCode) + EditorOptionsDialog Code Features tab toggle; the active GrammarDialect drives which lexer/highlighter is used.
Approach: a new pipeline stage that (1) matches the verb-list header via regex, (2) enters a 'capturing code' state, (3) strips ANSI from each captured line (AnsiManager), (4) tokenizes via the dialect lexer and maps tokens to the editor color scheme, (5) emits the recolored line to the terminal renderer (RTF/HTML), (6) exits capture on termination.
OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (resolve via brainstorming before implementing):
 1. TERMINATION DETECTION (the hard part the user flagged): how to know the code listing ended. Options to evaluate: a trailing blank line / the next command prompt, @list line-number prefixes (count/format), a known end-of-listing marker, or a heuristic 'first line that doesn't lex as continued code / matches a prompt'. ToastStunt/LambdaMOO @list output has no explicit terminator, so this needs a robust heuristic.
 2. Exact header regex incl. quoted verb names, multiple aliases, optional/variant flag and owner formats across dialects/cores.
 3. Whether @program echo and other code-listing commands (not just @list) should also trigger.
 4. Interaction with existing ANSI/color pipeline and mobile-wrap/nowrap (SDWC-START/END-NOWRAP) handling.
 5. Performance: highlighting per-line in the terminal stream without lag.
 6. How re-coloring composes with the terminal's RTF/HTML rendering path (PlainTextToHtmlConverter / ExportToRTF).
acceptance_criteria: Toggle on Options > Code Features (default off). With it on, a verb listing in the terminal that starts with the standard verb-list header has its code body shown with editor syntax highlighting, with the MOO's own ANSI coloring stripped first; listing termination is detected so normal (non-code) output afterward is unaffected. With it off, terminal output is unchanged. Lexing uses the session's GrammarDialect. Build clean; tests for the header matcher, ANSI stripping, and termination heuristic.

title: Smart brackets: line-balance auto-close + whitespace-tolerant auto-delete (incl. escape-aware quotes)
description: Enhance the EXISTING auto-bracket behavior (FCTB DoAutocompleteBrackets + MooCodeEditor backspace handler, gated by AutoCompleteBrackets/EditorAutoBrackets) for the bracket pairs () [] {}. Two refinements: (1) when typing an opener, only insert the matching closer if the current line does not already have an unmatched closer ahead that this opener would balance; (2) when backspacing an opener, also delete the matching closer when it is the first non-whitespace char ahead on the same line, removing the intervening whitespace too. Quotes are intentionally out of scope for both refinements.
design:
EXISTING: FCTB.DoAutocompleteBrackets (FastColoredTextBox.cs:4892) always inserts the pair on an opener (plus type-over when next char==closer); MooCodeEditor.MooEditor_KeyDown (MooCodeEditor.cs:458-467) deletes the closer on backspace ONLY when opener/closer are immediately adjacent (covers ()[]{} and quote).
R1 (auto-close suppression): OPT-IN property on the FCTB fork (default off, enabled only on MooCodeEditor so terminal/document editors keep current behavior). When typing opener L (matching R), scan current line from caret to EOL tracking depth (+1 L, -1 R); if depth goes negative (unmatched closer ahead) insert only L, else insert the LR pair. Type-over/selection-wrap unchanged. ()[]{} only; quote auto-close unchanged (symmetric quote has no depth).
R2 (bracket whitespace-tolerant delete): extend MooEditor_KeyDown for ()[]{}: scan right from caret on same line skipping spaces/tabs; if first non-ws char is matching closer, remove opener+intervening whitespace+closer.
R3 (escape-aware quote delete, replaces current immediate-adjacency quote branch): on backspace of a quote, count consecutive backslashes immediately before it; if ODD the quote is escaped content -> normal backspace; if EVEN (incl 0, and \\") it is a delimiter -> scan right skipping ws, if first non-ws is a quote (necessarily unescaped) remove deleted-quote+whitespace+matching-quote (whitespace collapsed, same as brackets). A spaces-only string collapses fully (accepted). Escape via backslash PARITY, not just preceding-char==backslash.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-close: opener no unmatched closer ahead -> pair; opener with unmatched closer ahead -> only opener; type-over/wrap intact. Bracket delete: adjacent->both; ws-then-closer->opener+ws+closer; non-ws before closer->only opener. Quote delete: adjacent quote->both; ws-then-quote->both+ws; non-ws content before quote->only deleted quote; escaped \" (odd run)->normal backspace; \\" (even run)->delimiter. R1 off for terminal/document editors. Editor tests green; app builds clean.
close_reason: Implemented R1/R2/R3. Pure helpers SmartBracketDecisions.HasUnmatchedCloserAhead (FCTB, opt-in SmartBracketSuppressWhenUnbalanced, enabled only on MooCodeEditor) and SmartBracketDeletion.FindMatchingCloserAhead/IsUnescapedQuoteDelimiter (backslash parity). DoAutocompleteBrackets suppresses closer when unmatched closer ahead; MooEditor_KeyDown backspace removes opener+ws+closer for ()[]{} and escape-aware for quotes. 30 FCTB + 248 Editor tests pass. Merged to master.

title: Autocomplete: core-reference ($) completion lists #0 verbs, not just properties
description: When the user types '$', completion currently lists only #0's properties (FetchMemberListAsync routes CoreReference to GetPropertiesAsync). But '$foo()' is a valid verb call on #0, so '$' completion should also list #0's verbs with the verb icon. Less common usage but legitimate.
design: In FetchMemberListAsync (MemberCompletionController.cs:573-580), for MemberContextKind.CoreReference fetch BOTH GetPropertiesAsync and GetVerbsAsync on #0 and merge: properties via BuildPropertyItems (CoreReference icon), verbs via BuildVerbItems (Verb icon). #0 may have a property AND verb of the same name ($foo reads prop, $foo() calls verb) — emit BOTH; FCTB DoAutocomplete does not dedup by text. Core-ref verb items reuse the paren-insertion from udd-16x (so depends on udd-16x). Existing CoreReference property behavior and TTL caching preserved; only the fetched set widens.
acceptance_criteria: Typing '$' lists #0 properties (core icon) AND #0 verbs (verb icon). A name present as both prop and verb shows two entries. Selecting a core-ref verb inserts name() cursor-between (via udd-16x). Editor tests green; app builds clean.
close_reason: Implemented: FetchMemberListAsync CoreReference branch fetches BOTH properties and verbs on #0, merges (core-icon props + verb-icon VerbCompletionItem with paren insertion); same-name prop+verb both listed. . and : paths unchanged; TTL caching preserved. 248 Editor tests pass. Merged to master.

title: Autocomplete: insert verbs as name() with cursor between parens
description: When a user selects a verb from autocomplete (member verb via ':' or core-reference verb via '$'), insert 'verbname()' and place the cursor between the parens, matching the existing built-in-function snippet behavior. Today BuildVerbItems (MemberCompletionController) emits MemberCompletionItem(name,icon) which inserts the bare name. Properties and core-reference PROPERTIES stay bare (not callable) — only verbs get parens.
design: Make verb items snippet-capable so selection inserts 'name(^)' (FCTB caret marker ^), cursor between parens, regardless of verb arity (arity not known from MooVerbSummary — accepted). Change BuildVerbItems to emit a snippet-style item (mirror how Moo.Builtins arg-taking functions use 'name(^)' built in Moo.cs static ctor). Built-in functions already do this: arg-taking -> 'name(^)' (cursor between), no-arg -> 'name()^' (cursor after) — LEFT AS-IS, not unified. Property/CoreReference-property items unchanged (bare name). Reused by udd-afl-sibling core-ref verb listing bead.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a member verb inserts 'verbname()' with caret between parens. Properties still insert bare names. Built-in function insertion unchanged. Editor tests green; app builds clean.
close_reason: Implemented: verbs insert name() with caret between parens via new VerbCompletionItem; BuildVerbItems emits it. Properties/core-ref props and builtins unchanged. 244 Editor tests pass. Merged to master (5760879).

title: Autocomplete: harvest all verb variable names into non-member completion list
description: Discover every variable-position identifier in the verb's parse tree and inject them as Variable-icon entries into the non-member (identifier-prefix) completion list. Flat lexical harvest — NO flow/branch/reachability reasoning (that is udd-2s4's job) and NO value resolution; names only. Distinct from udd-2s4: this lists names, udd-2s4 resolves a name's current value. Builds on the same parse-tree snapshot already passed to completion (MemberCompletionContextSnapshot.Tree + caret).
design: New pure static VariableReferenceCollector.CollectVariableNames(ParserRuleContext? tree, int caretOffset) in Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Editor/Autocomplete/, reusing FlowValueResolver's Walk traversal. Collects every identifier in a VARIABLE position (NOT the member name right of ./: and not a call name), dedup case-insensitive, preserve as-written. Excludes the in-progress identifier occurrence under/left of caret UNLESS the same name occurs elsewhere as a variable (no self-referential noise). Dynamic per-keystroke collection in DynamicCompletionSource.GetEnumerator() using snapshot.Tree+caret. Asymmetric dedup vs statics: SUPPRESS names matching Moo.Keywords (built-in variables this/player/caller/args, constants, control-flow — keyword entry already IS the variable); DO NOT suppress names matching built-in FUNCTIONS Moo.Builtins (a local var shadowing read() is meaningful -> emit BOTH, distinct icons; FCTB DoAutocomplete does not dedup by text). Wrap survivors with CompletionIconCategory.Variable, merge-sort with already-sorted static list, yield alphabetically. Member items unchanged; matching stays closest-match (framework). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-variable-completion-harvesting-design.md
acceptance_criteria: VariableReferenceCollector unit tests: plain/compound/scatter targets, for-loop vars, except vars, bare read refs, name-as-member-vs-variable, caret-exclusion rule. Dedup tests: name==keyword suppressed; name==builtin function emits both. Full Editor test suite green; app builds clean.
close_reason: Implemented: new VariableReferenceCollector.CollectVariableNames (tree walk, variable-position = IdentifierExpressionContext + for/except/scatter targets; caret occurrence excluded unless used elsewhere; case-insensitive dedup). DynamicCompletionSource.GetEnumerator harvests dynamically per refresh, asymmetric dedup (suppress Moo.Keywords, keep Moo.Builtins functions), merged alphabetically. 280 Editor tests pass (18 new). Merged to master.

title: Autocomplete: multi-step chained-expression evaluation for HOVER tooltips
description: Follow-up to udd-efk. Completion resolves full chains ($Mcp.package:) but hover tooltips resolve only single-atom operands. The hover operand detector MooCodeEditor.ClassifyHoveredMember emits a single token, so ResolveHoverOperandAsync (already routed through ChainExpressionEvaluator) never receives multi-step chains. Extend ClassifyHoveredMember to walk left and capture the full chain (reuse ChainExtractor), then feed base+steps into the evaluator so hovering a member on $Mcp.package:foo resolves the same way completion does. Design already specifies hover parity; this closes that gap.
close_reason: Multi-step chained-expression evaluation for hover tooltips implemented: new ChainExtractor.ExtractAtSeparator captures the full chain to the left of the hovered member (tree-primary, token fallback); MooCodeEditor.ClassifyHoveredMember threads base+steps + a local-variable resolver through MooHoverRequest; page resolves the chain via ChainExpressionEvaluator (full parity with completion, including variable bases). Swallowed extraction exceptions logged via injected HoverDiagnostic -> Logger.Warn. 199 tests pass (6 new), app builds clean.

title: Autocomplete: flow-aware lazy reassignment tracking for this/player/caller + locals
description: Follow-up to udd-efk (chained-eval). Resolve the value of a variable used DIRECTLY under the caret (not just as a chain base) when it has been reassigned earlier in the verb, e.g. 'player = #23; ... player:' should complete on #23. Requires a fuller statement-level interpretation of the verb's parse tree along the path from verb start to caret, tracking current values of this/player/caller and arbitrary locals, including branch-reachability awareness (which assignment actually executes). Builds on udd-efk's ChainExpressionEvaluator/LocalVariableResolver/ChainExtractor and reuses the same per-step provider resolution and no-source fallback. Ambiguous/unknown -> no source.
design: Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-flow-aware-value-tracking-design.md. Approach: new pure FlowValueResolver (linear pre-caret, three-state Unmodified/Reassigned/Ambiguous; definite-path vs conditional-branch vs loop-back-edge conservatism; offset-correct nested-snapshot reduction) supersedes LocalVariableResolver as the evaluator's value source. ChainExpressionEvaluator consults it once per top-level this/player/caller/local base, then resolves a fully-reduced GROUND chain (keyword base = default). Wired into completion (controller incl. sync cache path) + hover; adds bare-local hover (deferred from udd-3y3). Decisions: ambiguous keyword -> default, ambiguous/unassigned local -> unknown; hover label 'no source' -> '(unknown source)'. Out: loop fixpoint, scatter assignment.
notes: Bare this/player/caller (and #N) HOVER tooltip was split out to udd-3y3 (fix-first, default resolution). udd-2s4 remains the flow-aware reassignment-tracking FEATURE; it will later layer reassignment-aware values onto the udd-3y3 hover path AND the under-caret completion path.
close_reason: Implemented flow-aware lazy reassignment tracking. New pure FlowValueResolver (linear pre-caret, three-state Unmodified/Reassigned/Ambiguous; definite-path vs conditional-branch vs loop-back-edge conservatism; offset-correct nested-snapshot reduction incl. keyword RHS bases; all assignment forms — plain/compound/scatter; scatter resolves a plain target's positional element when it is an explicit object reference, reducing the RHS to a list literal even through a variable indirection a={$mcp,5};{mcp,count}=a) supersedes LocalVariableResolver. ChainExpressionEvaluator consults it once per top-level this/player/caller/local base then resolves a fully-reduced ground chain (keyword base=default). Wired into completion (controller async + sync cache path) and hover; adds bare-local hover (deferred from udd-3y3); hover label 'no source'->'(unknown source)'. pack=$mcp.package;pack: resolves like $mcp.package:. Decisions: ambiguous keyword->default, ambiguous/unassigned local->unknown, compound-assigned keyword->unknown. Out: loop fixpoint, optional/rest scatter, chained-assignment RHS value. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-flow-aware-value-tracking-design.md. 234 Editor tests pass (incl. 35 FlowValueResolver), app builds clean. LocalVariableResolver removed; its tests migrated.

title: Autocomplete: chained member-access expression evaluation (+ minimal var-base tree walk)
description: Resolve chained member-access expressions at the caret so verb/property autocomplete AND hover offer the right object's members. Typing $Mcp.package: evaluates the chain $Mcp -> .package to a concrete object number, then completes members on it. Chain base may be #N, $name, this, player, caller, or a LOCAL VARIABLE. A local-variable base is resolved by a grammar-aware TREE WALK over the verb's ANTLR parse tree to its nearest preceding assignment (any block depth), whose RHS is itself evaluated as a full resolvable chain (recursive, with cycle + depth-8 guards). Three new Editor-library units: ChainExtractor (parse-tree-primary, token fallback), ChainExpressionEvaluator (async recursive), LocalVariableResolver (pure tree walk). Two-layer caching: world-state (objectId,propName) TTL-cached per page; local-variable values NEVER cached (re-derived from live parse tree each request). Swallowed exceptions logged via the existing diagnostic delegate -> Logger.Warn; expected non-resolution stays silent. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-chained-expression-evaluation-design.md
notes: Enhancement: the interpreter should also evaluate CHAINED member-access expressions to an object as the completion source. E.g. typing '$Mcp.package:' should evaluate '$Mcp.package' over the current connection (resolve $Mcp -> #0.Mcp's object value, then read property '.package' on that object); if the result is an object number, use that # as the source to fetch available verbs/properties for. So the walker resolves operand chains of the form <base>.prop[.prop...] where <base> may be $name / #N / this / player / caller / a local variable, evaluating each step via the provider's property-value query, then completes members on the final resolved object. Non-object / unresolved steps fall back to no-source.
close_reason: Chained member-access expression evaluation implemented + user-verified working in connected app ($Mcp.package: resolves through $Mcp->#221, .package->#215, lists #215 verbs). Includes minimal var-base tree walk, two-layer caching, exception-logging split. Root-cause fix: async menu re-open guard now threads full tree/tokens/caret context (was line-prefix-only, which couldn't extract multi-segment chains). 193 tests pass. Completion done; chained hover deferred (udd-2s4 is the flow-aware reassignment follow-up; chained-hover filed separately).

title: IMcpPackage interface polish: read-only Name/version properties, Reset() contract
description: Inherited 2022-era design flaws noted in udd-btl Task 6 review: (1) IMcpPackage.Name/MinimumVersion/MaximumVersion are get;set; — mutating Name would desynchronize the dispatcher registration key from the const PackageName each package matches on in CanHandleMessage; should be get-only. (2) Reset() exists on packages with <inheritdoc/> but is not declared on IMcpPackage or IMcpProtocolHandler and is never called — either add it to the interface (and call on disconnect, see related teardown bug) or delete it everywhere.

value: When a change removes or alters a PUBLIC behavior/registration path (not just internal logic), run the FULL solution test suite (dotnet test on the .sln), not just the directly-changed project's tests. Cross-project tests exercise these paths: e.g. udd-3w0 removed SdwcOobHandler's dome-client-user registration path and the merge verification only ran Communication.Tests, but DisconnectTeardownCascadeTests live in Org.Edgerunner.Mud.MCP.Tests and registered the SDWC provider via dome-client-user -> 2 silent regressions shipped+closed. Merge/close checklist for behavior-altering changes: dotnet test the whole solution.

Workflow: close the relevant bead BEFORE committing, so the bead-state change (.beads/issues.jsonl) lands in the SAME commit as the code/work it relates to. Do not commit the code first and close the bead afterward — that strands the bead closure (and any follow-on label/archive changes) in separate trailing commits.

Autocomplete menu re-open gotcha (chained completion): when an async member-completion fetch lands after the FCTB popup closed, the re-open guard in MooCodeEditorPage must call MemberCompletionController.GetMemberItems with the SAME full context (parse Tree/Tokens/CaretLine/CaretColumn via GetMemberCompletionContext) that DynamicCompletionSource.GetEnumerator uses. The line-prefix-only GetMemberItems overload falls into ChainExtractor.ExtractFromLinePrefix, which resolves single-atom (length-1) chains only — so multi-segment chains ($Mcp.package:) get Count==0 and the popup never re-opens even though verbs were fetched+cached. Symptom: single-atom completion works, chained completion shows NO popup, but the NLog log shows the prop-value/verbs OOB replies arriving. Any code path that gates the popup on item count must thread the live tree, not just the line prefix.

Design rule (Thad, emphatic): verb/property SUMMARY listings (GetVerbsAsync/GetPropertiesAsync and any wire payloads behind them) care about the QUERIED object only — do NOT carry or design in per-row defining-object data. Client-side summary records fill DefiningObject with the queried object id. Resolved/defining-object semantics are legitimate ONLY where the IMooWorldQueryProvider contract explicitly models them: GetVerbInfoAsync, GetVerbDocumentationAsync, GetVerbCodeAsync (QueriedObjectId/ResolvedObjectId pairs).

isolation:worktree subagents branch from origin/master (last PUSHED commit), NOT current local HEAD. If local master has merged-but-unpushed work, a subagent dispatched to stack a fix on that work will silently get the STALE origin base (missing the merged features) and produce a branch that conflicts/regresses on merge. Seen 2026-06-26: a udd-7wl fix agent branched from 4b7d174 (docs-only origin) lacking VerbCompletionItem, so its branch was discarded and the fix applied inline on local master. Mitigation: PUSH local master before dispatching worktree subagents that must build on already-merged work; or apply stacked fixes inline. Independent (non-stacked) parallel features are fine since their branches merge cleanly onto local master.

NEVER 'rm -rf' a project's bin/ output directory. The app's ResolveDataFile falls back to AppDomain.BaseDirectory (bin/Debug|Release/net6.0-windows) for runtime data files like Worlds.xml (the saved-connections AddressBook), which are NOT csproj content and are therefore NOT regenerated by a build. On 2026-06-26 'rm -rf Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor/bin/Debug' (done to clear a stale .resources for an MSB3577 error) deleted the user's bin/Debug Worlds.xml; user had to restore it. To clear stale build state use 'dotnet clean' or delete ONLY obj/ (or the single stale file). For MSB3577 specifically, only obj/Debug needs clearing. Treat bin/ as potentially containing irreplaceable user runtime data.

Build gotcha (Udditor): VS sometimes auto-creates an empty boilerplate .resx for a hand-written FORM PARTIAL file (e.g. Main/Editor_ViewMenu.resx for the partial class Editor). Because it resolves to the same manifest name as the form's real resx (Main/Editor.resx -> Org.Edgerunner.Moo.Udditor.Main.Editor.resources), the build fails with MSB3577 'Two output file names resolved to the same output path'. These empty resx files are usually UNTRACKED (never committed), so fresh clones build fine and 'dotnet test' on the solution doesn't catch it (no test project references the Udditor app). Fix: delete the spurious empty partial resx (it only contains the commented schema examples Name1/Color1/Bitmap1/Icon1, no real <data name="$this"> entries). Only the form's own resx (Editor.resx) should exist.

Color-picker gotcha (magenta): magenta (FF00FF) is commonly used as a transparency MASK key in WinForms/GDI. On a prior project, a color swatch BUTTON whose BackColor was set to magenta rendered transparent, and the ColorDialog broke when seeded from it. Mitigation pattern used in ThemeEditorDialog: the swatch is an owner-drawn ColorSwatch control that paints the color via SolidBrush in OnPaint (never via control BackColor), and the ColorDialog is seeded from the stored setting value (get()), not from the swatch control. For any NEW color-picker UI, do NOT drive a swatch fill through a control's BackColor and do NOT seed the ColorDialog from the control -- otherwise magenta will render/behave as transparent.

net6->net8 (net8.0-windows) WinForms breaking changes hit in this repo after the retarget: (1) System.Reflection.MethodInvoker (new in net8) collides with System.Windows.Forms.MethodInvoker -> CS0104 build errors in FastColoredTextBox.cs; fixed with 'using MethodInvoker = System.Windows.Forms.MethodInvoker;'. (2) KeysConverter on net8 only accepts full Keys enum names, NOT the old abbreviations Ins/Del/PgUp/PgDn -> ArgumentException 'Requested value Ins was not found' at runtime when any FCTB control is constructed (HotkeysMapping.Parse); fixed by normalizing those abbreviations in Parse. LESSON: the app/Udditor has no test project and the WinForms UI isn't unit-tested, so net8 runtime regressions (designer/resx/serialized-string parsing) can pass the build+test suite and only surface when the app runs. After framework retargets, exercise the running app (open a terminal, open/load/save a file, options dialog) to catch these.
